name: Technology assessment
problem: An assessment of a new technology ends up as reports, interviews and scenario notes, or as boxes in a general-purpose whiteboard, where options, actors and consequences sit apart. A specialized view shows who expects what and which trade-offs follow, so the assessment can be argued over instead of read front to back.

name: Humans and agents together
problem: When people and agents work together, what each is doing lives in prompts, task lists, logs and chat, or in a generic board neither was built for. A specialized view shows the shared work as tasks, owners and states, so a person sees at a glance what an agent did and why, and the agent reads the same file.

name: Clarity in textual data
problem: Logs, notes and plain-text formats hide their structure in line after line, and a general-purpose editor shows them only as lines. A specialized view shows the hierarchy, the repetition and the outliers directly, while the text stays the source of truth and still reads as text.

name: Systems and strategy
problem: Strategies and system descriptions are written as prose and bullet lists, or drawn as boxes and arrows in a generic diagram tool, and neither shows how feedback, dependencies and position work. A specialized view draws the loops, value chains and landscapes as they are, so a decision can be traced to the structure behind it.

name: Knowledge and semantics
problem: Ontologies, vocabularies and linked data are graphs written down as text, and a general-purpose editor shows the lines but not the links in which their meaning lives. A specialized view draws the classes, concepts and relations, so a model can be checked by eye while the file stays the standard.

name: Software delivery
problem: Pipelines, deployments and dependencies are spread over many configuration files, and a generic diagram of them is out of date the day after it is drawn. A specialized view draws the delivery from the files themselves, as it runs, so a change can be understood before it ships.

name: Planning and roadmapping
problem: Plans kept as lists and documents lose time, order and what waits on what, and a general-purpose chart has to be redrawn with every change. A specialized view places the work on a timeline straight from its text and draws its dependencies, so overlaps and critical paths show at a glance.

name: Psychological and societal insights
problem: How people and societies respond to change is recorded in articles, surveys and observations, and a generic chart flattens it to a single line. A specialized view lays out hype, adoption and feedback in behaviour side by side, so patterns can be discussed rather than assumed.
